# 17 Fix the top participant row overlapping the first message

## Outcome

The top participant box sits in the vertical band `layoutSequence` reserves for it, above every
message, instead of overlapping the first message row. Every message, block frame, and destroy
mark still falls below the top row and above the bottom row.

## Why this ticket exists

Found while closing ticket 15. `layoutSequence` reserves the top row's height *above*
`lifelineTop`, but `renderSequenceToSVG` draws the top box *downward from* `participant.top`, so
the box occupies `[top, top + height]` — the same band the first message is laid into. The bottom
row is already handled the other way (`participant.bottom - participant.height`, i.e. inside its
reserved band), so the two rows are inconsistent with each other.

Reproduced on the simplest possible document (`participant A`, `participant B`,
`A->>B: first message`): the top box spans y 56–112 and the message path is at y 96 — drawn
inside the box. Every sequence diagram is affected, including the three committed demo examples.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a two-participant, one-message document, the top participant box's bottom edge is at or
  above the first message's y — no overlap.
- [ ] The same holds when the first message is nested inside a block (the block frame's top edge
  is also at or below the top row's bottom edge).
- [ ] Each `<line class="siren-lifeline">` still starts at its participant's box (its `y1` is
  unchanged relative to the box it hangs from) and ends where its extent says.
- [ ] The bottom participant row's geometry is unchanged — it already sits inside its reserved
  band, and the returned `height` still contains it.
- [ ] A `create`d participant's single box likewise does not overlap the message row it was
  created at.
- [ ] Any existing test asserting the old (overlapping) top-box y is updated in the same change,
  with its expectation corrected rather than loosened.

## Test seam

`layoutSequence(model, options): PositionedSequenceDiagram` (unit, fake `TextMeasurer`) and
`renderSequenceToSVG(diagram): SVGSVGElement` (component, jsdom); `render()` in
`index.test.ts` only if an end-to-end assertion is the clearest way to pin the no-overlap rule.
